rationale: A defensible economic re-specification of the archive's strongest signal (Post-Capex External Rescue) by swapping organic capex for M&A intensity, but it is a single-leg substitution on an established template, and TS_RANK of a lumpy, mostly-zero aqc series will produce heavy rank ties that blunt the investment leg.

The investment leg is effectively identical to the archived "Stockpiled-Capital Inventory Overhang" (TS_RANK of invt/at) and the financing leg is the same cash-consumed external-financing term used in three archived signals, so this is a recombination rather than a new mechanism; worse, TS_RANK of a highly persistent *level* mostly identifies chronically inventory-heavy firms rather than an overhang event.

The lag-then-finance sequencing with a debt-only funding leg is a coherent and non-mechanical variation on "Debt-Cash-Consumed Capex Peak," though TS_RANK of a one-year delta over only five annual observations is a noisy state variable and the expected incremental information over the archived version is modest.

Reversing the sequencing of the archived "Equity-Deleveraging Preinvestment Ramp" is a genuine timing test rather than a cosmetic tweak, the MIN(net equity issuance, debt retirement) construction correctly isolates simultaneous equity-in/debt-out firms, and the hypothesis and sign are internally consistent.

This is "Synchronous External Investment Peaks" with a single Δcash term subtracted, and that subtraction makes the financing leg approximate the sources-uses identity (external funds not parked in cash ≈ investment plus working capital less operating cash flow), so the two legs become mechanically overlapping rather than independently informative.

The fully lagged investment-plus-liquidity-depletion state interacted with contemporaneous issuance cleanly separates cause from funding and avoids the accounting identity that undermines several archived variants; the main weakness is that SUMRANK lets pure cash decliners with no investment score highly, diluting the intended "emergency financing" population.
